results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Bringer of the Last Gift, Superior Spider-Man and Town Greeter.
results.text:
I'll start by checking the three requested cards and what real decks play alongside them.

The three cards sit in different places: Town Greeter appears mainly in Golgari Roots lists, Superior Spider-Man in a Rogue list, and Bringer has no published lists. I'll check the current meta and the candidate shells.

The Golgari Roots list is a real self-mill shell that runs Town Greeter. Before choosing a direction, I need to see which mill and reanimation enablers are legal in Standard.

The Golgari Roots shell gives me a self-mill package to build from. Next I'll pull the self-mill cards and the Golgari core cards to confirm their text and legality.

Tyvar is not legal in Standard, so I'll leave it out. Next I'll confirm the mana, removal and creature options I'm considering.

Several removal spells I'd expect (Go for the Throat, Cut Down, Tear Asunder, Sheoldred's Edict) are not legal here, so I'll build around Bitter Triumph, Shoot the Sheriff, Maelstrom Pulse and Quag Feast. Next I'll look at the Golgari Midrange shell for a proven removal and creature suite.

Golgari Roots and Golgari Midrange together give me the mana, mill and removal core. I'll check the remaining sideboard candidates and the blue splash odds before building the list.

Two findings change the plan. Screaming Nemesis is banned in Standard, so the Izzet and Boros lists in the menu are out of date. Blue splash math is workable: 5 blue sources gives a 69% chance of seeing one by turn 6. Now I'll check the full draft against the Golgari Roots mana base.

The checker passes with no errors. The only warning is green sources (15.5 against the Golgari Roots norm of about 21), which is the cost of splashing blue for Spider-Man. I'll accept it and explain it. Submitting now.

The submission was rejected only because the blue splash has 5 sources, below the 6 the checker expects for a build-around. I'll keep the 5 sources and give the reason, since the draw odds support that and the blue sources double as mill lands.

The checker flagged Coati Scavenger as a card players rarely choose. In this deck it has a specific job, so I'll keep it and answer the note.

I built a Golgari self-mill deck with a blue splash for Superior Spider-Man. It fills the graveyard with Town Greeter, Molt Tender, Overlord of the Balemurk and Dredger's Insight, then uses Overlord and Spider-Man to copy and recur creatures until Bringer of the Last Gift can return the whole pile on turn 8.

I chose this direction over a Dimir build that would drop Town Greeter, because only the Golgari Roots shell mills enough to make Bringer's graveyard full; Dimir would have only Restless Reef as a mill source. The main caveat is consistency: the win line is only drawn by turn 8 in about 7% of games, and Bringer needs ramp to reach 8 mana. The deck is also short on green sources (about 12 real G sources) because of the blue splash.

Two things to know about the meta data. Screaming Nemesis is banned in Standard, so the Izzet and Boros lists in the menu are out of date. Four of Golgari's sideboard-style removal spells I checked are also not legal here, so I built the removal around Bitter Triumph, Shoot the Sheriff, Maelstrom Pulse and Quag Feast.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Mightform Harmonizer, Spell Snare and Full Bore.
results.text:
The deck is submitted as a brew: a green-blue ramp list with a red splash for Full Bore. I took the Simic Ouroboroid mana base and ramp package as the shell, because Mightform Harmonizer (green), Spell Snare (blue) and Full Bore (red) don't appear together in any published list. I chose this over an R/G warp-landfall build, which would have dropped Spell Snare, and over a U/R warp build, which would have dropped Mightform.

The plan is to ramp with Llanowar Elves and cast Mightform Harmonizer warped for 2G on turn 4. Then play a land to double its power to 8, and cast Full Bore for haste and trample to attack for about 11. The deck runs 23 lands, including 3 Mountains and 2 Multiversal Passages for red, and Gene Pollinator can also help cast Full Bore.

The main weakness is the red splash: Full Bore has only about 5 red sources, below the roughly 14 it wants to be cast on curve. The exact turn-4 line completes in only about 1.4% of games, so this is a flexible midrange deck, not a reliable turn-4 kill. I swapped out both Close Encounter copies, which almost no recent decks run, for Repulsive Mutation and Tishana's Tidebinder.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Airbender Ascension, Bramble Familiar and Appa, Steadfast Guardian.
results.text:

I sketched three directions. A GWU Rogue list would be the closest proven shell, since most real lists with Appa and Bramble are Rogue, but it adds blue and a messier mana base. A Selesnya Ouroboroid build with the airbend cards was the strongest, and an all-Ally build had too little power. I went with the Selesnya build because Ouroboroid is the best-performing engine in the green lists, and the airbend suite gives tempo, flicker value and removal without splashing.

The plan is to ramp into Ouroboroid, Innkeeper's Talent and Aang while using Airbender Ascension and Appa to remove blockers and reuse Bramble Familiar and Sentinel for extra value. The stated win line (Bramble, then Ascension, then Appa flash, then Ouroboroid, then Talent) is only in hand by turn 6 in about 0.6% of games, so treat it as a rough plan rather than a reliable kill. Appa is legendary, so I ran three copies. The deck is 21 lands with 8 mana creatures, below the checker's recommended 23, which I accepted because the curve is low.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Ashling, Rekindled, Sunderflock and Bounce Off.
results.text:
The deck is accepted as a brew. It is an Izzet Elemental deck built around Sunderflock, with Ashling and Bounce Off as the core.

**Plan:** Ashling turns on Rimebound mana for the 4+ drops, Flamebraider adds mana for Elemental spells, and nearly every creature is an Elemental. Eddymurk Crab (MV 7) or another high-MV Elemental cuts Sunderflock's cost to a few mana, and its ETB bounces only the opponent's non-Elementals. Torch the Tower, Burst Lightning and Bounce Off handle early threats.

**Direction:** I weighed three options. A Simic Ouroboroid shell with Bounce Off would have no Elementals for Sunderflock to count and no red for Ashling. A blue-only Elemental control deck would lose Ashling's ramp and the burn package. The UR Elemental build uses all three requested cards, so I chose it.

**Caveats:**
- No published list runs these cards together, so this is a brew. The mana base and burn package borrow from Rogue and Izzet results.
- Summon: Shiva has 0% play in recent Standard lists. I kept it because it is an Elemental with MV 5 that helps cut Sunderflock's cost. The checker flagged it, and I answered that in the submission.
- Stormchaser's Talent appears in the Lessons and Prowess lists on the menu, but card lookup shows it banned in Standard, so I left it out.
- Odds are rough: Ashling is in hand or drawn by turn 3 about 49% of the time on the play, and the turn-5 win line is far from reliable.

results.prompt: Brew me a Standard deck built around Iron-Shield Elf, Bloodthorn Flail and Flamewake Phoenix.
results.text:
I built a black-red aggro deck around all three cards: Iron-Shield Elf and Bloodthorn Flail are black, and Flamewake Phoenix is red. I considered three directions: a Boros (red-white) build borrowing the Boros Aggro list, which would drop two of your three cards; an Izzet build, which only fits the Phoenix; and this black-red build, which keeps all three. I borrowed the red core from Boros Aggro (Hired Claw, Emberheart Challenger, Burst Lightning, Lightning Strike, Torch the Tower).

The plan is to curve out with cheap creatures and burn, then put Bloodthorn Flail on Flamewake Phoenix to make it a 4/3 flyer with haste. Power 4 also turns on ferocious, so the Phoenix can return from the graveyard for R when it dies. Sunspine Lynx and Nova Hellkite are the other power-4 enablers, and Burst Lightning and Lightning Strike finish the game.

Things to know:
- **Mana is thin on paper.** The deck runs 17 lands (13 red, 10 black sources) with an average mana value of about 2.1. The checker recommends about 23.7 lands for that average, but the cheap curve, Phoenix recursion and Burst Lightning kicker keep 17 workable. Expect some mana trouble.
- **The win line is slow.** The full line of Challenger, Phoenix, Flail and Burst by turn 5 appears in only about 6.7% of games. The deck is a brew, so treat it as a playable starting point rather than a proven list.
- **One card changed.** The checker flagged Murder as almost unplayed in Standard, so I swapped it for Bitter Triumph, which is far more common and also hits planeswalkers.

The Legacy Sewer lists run Painter's Servant and Grindstone, which cannot be used here. The blue-red loop with the Lurrus Control interaction package was the strongest, since it is the only one where the three cards win by themselves.

**Honest odds:** Drawing all three combo pieces by turn 5 from the opening hand and draws alone is about 16%. The full winning sequence is drawn by turn 5 in about 3% of games. The tutors and cantrips raise that, but this is a fragile three-card combo and will often not go off on the first try.

**Checks:** The deck passes the format check at 60 cards. Ichor Wellspring and Cryogen Relic are kept on purpose, since they draw a card each time Welder sacrifices them. The checker's warning about only 8 lands is expected here, since the deck runs 13 other mana sources.

results.prompt: Brew me a Pauper deck built around Aurora Eidolon, Sandstorm Eidolon and Spirit Mascot.
results.text:
The deck is submitted as a Boros brew (17 lands are not used; it runs 18). It's built around Spirit Mascot, which grows whenever cards leave your graveyard. Battle Screech and Prismatic Strands flashbacks, Pursue the Past, and the Eidolons returning to hand all feed it. **Direction chosen:** Boros flashback aggro. I considered three directions:

2. **Mono-white with the Eidolons splashed:** not viable, since Sandstorm needs R and the recursion needs a multicolored spell, which needs both colors.

- None of the three cards appears in any tracked list, so this is a brew, not a proven deck.

**Line:** Spirit Mascot on turn 2, Skyknight Legionnaire on turn 3, then Battle Screech on turn 4, flashed back by tapping the birds and Mascot. Sandstorm Eidolon can make a blocker unable to block, and Lightning Bolt finishes, for a turn-5 win in the best case.

Buried Alive, Gravedigger-style recursion and the big black creatures are the key pieces. Next I'll confirm the exact text and legality of the candidate cards in one batch.

Mono-black Living Death is legal and the card pool has enough enablers: Buried Alive for mill, Putrid Imp and Cabal Therapy for discard, and Reanimate, Animate Dead and Exhume for returns. Next I'll check sideboard candidates and draw odds for the main line.

I built a mono-black Living Death deck. It is a brew, not a stock list: no tournament list runs this exact build, and Living Death appears in only about 0.3% of recent Premodern results.

Plan: turn 3 Buried Alive mills up to three fat creatures (Visara, Gargantua, Delver) into the graveyard, then turn 5 Living Death returns them and wipes the opponent's board. Putrid Imp, Gravedigger, Animate Dead and Reanimate add fuel and redundancy.

- **BG Survival with Living Death.** It would borrow Survival of the Fittest and Birds from the menu, but it spreads mana across two colors and Survival is slow.

Honest odds: Living Death is in hand by turn 5 on the play 56.6% of the time. The full win line (Buried Alive, Living Death, Gargantua, Visara all drawn) comes together by turn 5 only about 2% of the time, so expect games to go longer.
